## Last week vs. this week

- Last week: random intercepts — each group gets its own baseline
- This week: what if the **effect itself** varies by group, and what
  happens with more complex grouping structures?

## Random slopes

- `lmer(response ~ treatment + (treatment | site), data = ...)`
- Lets the treatment effect itself vary from site to site
- Compare to the random-intercept-only model with `anova()` — does
  allowing varying slopes meaningfully improve the fit?

## Nested random effects

- One factor's levels only make sense within another
  (e.g., `plot` within `site` — "plot 1" at Site A isn't the same
  physical plot as "plot 1" at Site B)
- Syntax: `(1 | site/plot)`

## Crossed random effects

- Levels of one factor occur across multiple levels of another
  (e.g., the same `observer` measures animals at several sites)
- Syntax: `(1 | site) + (1 | observer)`

## Telling them apart

- Ask: does "level 1" mean the same thing across every group?
  - Yes → crossed
  - No → nested
- Getting this wrong doesn't always error — it silently gives you the
  wrong model

## Putting it together

- Design (Weeks 5–6) → naive vs. blocked model (Week 5) → mixed model
  with random intercepts (Week 12) → random slopes and
  crossed/nested structures (today)
- Same underlying idea the whole way: account for the structure in
  how your data were collected
